title: Akzidenz Ordnung — Swiss Conference Statement
description: A strict International Typographic Style layout for academic talks: eight invisible columns, three fixed type sizes, and a single red rule at optical center — nothing else. Where most minimalist templates strip ornament but keep flexibility, this one enforces the grid as law.
philosophy: This template exists to serve the argument, not the speaker. It borrows directly from Müller-Brockmann's belief that structure is not a constraint but a form of respect — for the audience's attention and the content's rigor. It refuses gradient, color mood, decorative spacing, and any type size outside the defined triad. It is built for speakers who trust their theorems enough to let Helvetica carry them into a dim conference hall.
goodFor: Theoretical computer science or mathematics conference talks
Single-idea slides with a definition, lemma, or proof block
Academic keynotes where print-design credibility matters
3-line pull quotes or theorem statements needing visual authority
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly reviews requiring color-coded data series
Sales or pitch decks where brand warmth is expected
Slide sets with more than three levels of information hierarchy
Audiences unfamiliar with modernist typographic conventions
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide carries the austerity of a Müller-Brockmann exhibition poster brought into a dim lecture hall: severe, load-bearing, and entirely self-possessed. A single taut horizontal rule cleaves the composition, producing deliberate asymmetric tension — the title asserts itself above with near-monumental weight while attribution below recedes with institutional restraint. Negative space is not luxury; it is the argument. Avoid any centered symmetry, softened edge, or decorative spacing rhythm — the grid is the only ornament this slide is permitted.

examples.layoutNotes: Eight invisible columns govern all placement; title text sits flush left across columns 1–7, with column 8 held as hard structural silence. The template's single accent-colored horizontal rule spans the full column measure at optical center — approximately three-eighths down the slide height — and functions as the only non-typographic mark on the canvas. The talk title is set in the largest of the three permitted type sizes above the rule; conference name and presenter line cluster below in the smallest size, baseline-snapped to the shared grid unit. No decorative header band; a slide identifier or date anchors bottom-left, flush to column 1.

examples.promptCore: The slide reads like a page from a grid-systems manual transposed directly into a dim conference hall — cold, exacting, and entirely certain of itself. A lone horizontal rule divides the field, and the statement anchored below it carries the visual gravity of a published proof. Composition is flush-left and deliberately anti-expressive: no gestural spacing, no layered depth, no softness of any kind. Avoid decorative asymmetry, implied warmth, or any element introduced for visual interest rather than structural necessity.

examples.layoutNotes: Eight-column invisible grid anchors all content; the primary text block spans columns 1–6, with columns 7–8 held as structural void — not decorative whitespace, but enforced grid silence. A single horizontal rule at optical center bisects the slide, placing a compact section label or theorem tag above it and the dominant statement block — definition, lemma, or three-line pull quote — below. Hierarchy operates through three fixed type sizes only: micro-label, main statement body, and flush-left attribution or equation reference; all baseline-aligned with no vertical deviation. Page number sits bottom-right, outside the active column zone.
